transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Taylor Kim, Priya Desai, Marcus Lee, Alex Rivera, Sofia Nguyen, Jordan Patel, Maya Brooks, Evan Liu

Summary:
Medium-quality transcript of internal admin sync covering KMS rotation, service account audit, cost tagging for inference/Dedicated clusters, and minor legal/compliance notes. Agreed to run a small KMS rotation pilot and update runbooks; finance to adjust tagging for more accurate unit cost reporting.

Topics:
- KMS rotation / key management
- Service accounts / IAM cleanup
- Cost allocation tags for inference clusters (Dedicated/Hosted)
- Runbook updates and incident rollback steps
- Compliance questions (audit logs, retention)

Transcript:
[00:00] Taylor (IT): ok hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I think we're a little light on folks but enough to go through the admin items, welcome
[00:12] Priya (Finance Ops): yeah good morning, sorry had a payroll thing, should be fine for the next 40 minutes
[00:18] Marcus (Security): morning, Marcus here, i'll lead on the KMS discussion but quick note we already flagged a couple service accounts with overly broad roles
[00:28] Alex (Platform Admin): got it, Alex — i pulled the service-account export this morning, it's in the shared drive, link in the chat, caveat the map doesn't have some of the older Dedicated pools labeled
[00:39] Taylor: perfect, that helps, um first item KMS rotation — Marcus can you give the high level?
[00:45] Marcus: yeah so we're proposing quarterly rotations for non-prod and semi-annual for prod keys, there's a low risk window where we rotate primary key to secondary, test, then flip, but we need to verify model-serving KV cache persistence across rotations, and that Redwood runtime doesn't re-encrypt in-flight caches incorrectly, i've seen weird TTL behaviour in other runtimes
[01:07] Priya: what's the service impact window, like how long would requests see retries or failures?
[01:12] Marcus: ideally minutes, but worst case a brief spike in 5xx if the client libs are not re-fetching creds quickly; we can mitigate with a staggered rollout by region and Dedicated pool, plus a fallback to older key for a short period
[01:28] Taylor: ok so pilot — who owns pilot for a single Dedicated pool? Alex?
[01:33] Alex: happy to, i'll pick the staging dedicated pool in us-west2, run the rotation during off-hours and monitor the KV/cache hit ratios, i'll also coordinate with on-call to have rollback steps ready
[01:45] Marcus: i'll draft an impact analysis and a checklist — i'll include verification steps for prefix/KV cache and model serving paths, also add the tool-call edges that sometimes fail during re-encryption
[01:58] Taylor: great, put that in the shared doc, and Marcus, please add expected SLO degradation thresholds we accept
[02:04] Marcus: will do
[02:06] Priya: switching to finance ops — we're still seeing cost mis-attribution for inference tokens between Hosted and Dedicated, the tagging isn't uniform on some older clusters, which means our unit economics dashboard is off by about 8 to 12% this quarter
[02:21] Taylor: are those labels on the infra side or inside the runtime?
[02:25] Priya: mostly infra tags on the VM/pool and some pipeline tags from the model loader, both sides need standardization. i've added a spreadsheet with recommended tags and a mapping, link shared
[02:36] Jordan (Engineering): quick note, some of the older model variants have hard-coded tags in the deployment manifests — i'll sweep them in the next sprint but need a list of target clusters from Priya
[02:47] Priya: i'll export clusters and owners, and then we can triage by cost impact
[02:52] Marcus: also worth noting encryption-at-rest tags and key-owner fields, we should ensure the KMS key rotation plan is reflected in the cost allocation so we don't mischarge temporary storage costs during rotation windows
[03:07] Taylor: sounds reasonable. next item runbooks — Alex, you said you'd add rollback steps?
[03:12] Alex: yes, i'll append emergency rollback steps for model-serving deploys: cut traffic to canary, re-point to previous model variant, force KV cache invalidation if needed, and have a runbook note to check for 502/503 patterns that indicate decryption errors
[03:27] Sofia (Legal): on compliance, quick reminder we need to confirm retention for audit logs for Dedicated customers, the SOC2 mapping asks for X years of logs for certain controls, do we have a consistent retention policy?
[03:39] Marcus: we do for infra logs, but application-level request traces are on a different retention schedule depending on environment; we should standardize to at least 1 year for audit-relevant traces and keep longer for infra events
[03:52] Evan (Compliance): can you put the proposed retention durations in the shared compliance doc? i'll validate against SOC2 and ISO requirements, we may need to scope a separate retention tier for regulated customers
[04:03] Taylor: will do, Evan, include whether we need to purge older traces from the sandbox clusters
[04:09] Maya (HR): small ask from HR — when we rotate keys do we need to update any onboarding docs for service accounts? we've had a couple hires that couldn't access staging because roles changed
[04:19] Alex: good catch, yes update onboarding checklist, also include a note to request service-account access with the right tag so finance can tie costs
[04:27] Priya: i want to add a step: finance should be CC'd on service-account role changes that affect billing tags
[04:33] Taylor: agreed, add that to the action items
[04:36] Marcus: back to KMS, one technical item — the runtime currently caches the decrypted key material in memory for short TTL, we need to confirm memory clearing semantics at rotate; i'll add a verification step to the checklist to watch for stale key handles
[04:48] Jordan: and i'll run a quick smoke test where i force rekey and then run a series of short and long requests to check cache behavior
[04:56] Taylor: okay let's recap next steps and owners, Marcus you'll share the KMS plan, Alex does the pilot rotation, Priya updates the tagging sheet and shares cluster-owner list, Taylor will coordinate runbook updates and scheduling
[05:12] Priya: i'll also look at retroactive tag fixes for the last quarter so accounting can re-run cost allocations
[05:18] Sofia: i'll take a look at the retention and flag any legal constraints for dedicated customers
[05:24] Taylor: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the shared doc, and i propose a 30-min follow-up on 2026-07-09 to walk the runbook and pilot plan
[05:35] Alex: noted, i'll block calendar for tentative 07-09
[05:38] Marcus: added checklist items to the doc and flagged a few concerns in comments
[05:43] Taylor: cool, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
